purpose: Independent frozen-policy stress test of transfer when an old and a new rule share some, all, or none of their changing sensory coordinates.
construction: Keep B and its physical tapes identical. Rotate the A plane from the B plane into its orthogonal complement with equal principal angles. Regenerate the truly transformed A stimulus and matched-angle A query distractor, holding anchors, tastes, sides, clocks, filler requests and physical geometry fixed. The hidden angle is supplied only to the world builder.
endpoint: Describe early choice accuracy (mean of B2 and B4) and gate use after the first B receipt pair versus squared cosine of the hidden angle. Compare learned to best constant, full sharing and no sharing. Old first returns, joint choices and timeouts remain in the output. Root and birth bootstrap. No selection on these roots.
sign_intervention: For the learned gate, also replay the complete B gate schedule from the same-world twin with the same A signs and opposite B taste parity. Each recipient still learns from its own correct signed B tastes. The body, odors, history, and timing are matched. Use self gate on any unmatched write and report count. Quantifies sensitivity to the sign of reward in the gate, separately from contact-triggered sensory learning.
limits: Angles correspond to a controlled family of subspaces with equal principal angles. An independent random plane has a distribution of overlaps and is not the 90-degree endpoint. Near 90 degrees these worlds can penalize a poor fixed prior more than the random-unrelated arm of the main study.
